selected_hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive in open 4x4 vehicles to observe predator-prey interactions, lion prides, cheetahs, and elephants in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds, with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop. Spot hippos at Observation Hill, flamingos at Lake Amboseli, and diverse birdlife while experienced guides share deep knowledge of elephant family dynamics and ecosystems.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Participate in a guided rhino tracking experience on foot or by vehicle, meet rescued chimpanzees at the Jane Goodall sanctuary, and learn about critical conservation efforts protecting endangered species.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Five Safari
experiences.description: Discover Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its stunning flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park also offers excellent Big Five sightings including white and black rhinos, lions, leopards, and buffalos. Enjoy scenic viewpoints over the lake from Baboon Cliff for breathtaking panoramic photography.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village and Bush Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided visit to a traditional manyatta village near the Mara. Participate in traditional jumping dances, learn about ancient herding customs, medicinal plant knowledge, and beadwork craftsmanship. Follow a Maasai warrior guide on a bush walk to learn how indigenous communities have coexisted with wildlife for centuries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange shared shuttle or budget matatu transfer toward Narok (approximately 5–6 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Check in, freshen up, and take a short orientation walk around the camp grounds. Meet fellow travelers and staff to get tips for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport — budget KES 300–500 at airport kiosks.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple meal or grab a roadside chapati and beans at a local duka along the Narok highway — budget KES 150–250.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the camp's communal dining area. Ask for the budget set menu (ugali, sukuma wiki, grilled chicken) — budget KES 600–900.

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle in advance to save costs. Avoid private taxis from the airport as they are significantly more expensive. Carry KES cash as ATMs are scarce near the Mara.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 06:00 for your first budget game drive in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Join a shared group game drive (more affordable than private) and look for the Big Five — lions, elephants, leopards, buffalo, and rhino. The golden morning light is perfect for wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp by 10:30 for a late breakfast. Rest during the hottest part of the day. In the early afternoon, visit the Mara River viewpoint on foot (within camp vicinity) and watch for hippos and crocodiles from a safe distance along the riverbanks.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a cultural visit to a nearby Maasai village (manyatta). Learn about traditional Maasai customs, jumping dance, and beadwork. Many villages offer budget-friendly entrance fees around KES 500–800 per person.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast of mandazi, eggs, and chai tea — included or budget KES 300–400.
meals.lunch: Light packed lunch from camp — sandwiches, fruit, and juice — budget KES 200–350.
meals.dinner: Maasai village may offer a simple traditional meal, or return to camp for a budget communal dinner of nyama choma (grilled meat) and ugali — budget KES 700–1000.

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives. Bring a light fleece as early mornings can be cool even in July. Shared game drives typically cost KES 2,500–4,000 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start at 05:30 for a sunrise game drive focusing on predator activity — lions and cheetahs are most active at dawn. July is the beginning of the Great Wildebeest Migration season, so keep eyes peeled for massive herds moving through the reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp by 10:00. Spend the midday hours relaxing and journaling. At 14:00, take a self-guided nature walk around the camp perimeter with a camp guide (often free or low-cost) to learn about local flora, bird species, and smaller wildlife like mongoose and dik-dik.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner session on a hill near camp — bring your own snacks and drinks from camp supplies to keep costs low. Watch the spectacular African sunset over the savanna. Return to camp for a communal bonfire and stargazing session.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast — porridge, toast, and fresh fruit — budget KES 300–400.
meals.lunch: Simple camp lunch: rice and beans or lentil stew — budget KES 250–400.
meals.dinner: Communal camp dinner: vegetable curry and chapati — budget KES 600–800.

day_by_day.notes: July marks the start of the Great Migration — one of the world's most spectacular wildlife events. Ask your camp about the current wildebeest herd locations to plan drives accordingly. Binoculars are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day shared game drive starting at 06:00 into the heart of the Maasai Mara. Focus on the Mara Triangle area known for dense wildlife populations. Look for cheetah families, elephant herds, and giraffe on the open plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the full-day drive with a packed picnic lunch eaten at a designated scenic spot inside the reserve. Afternoon drives often yield great leopard sightings in acacia trees. Visit the famous Mara River crossing point to witness wildebeest attempting crossings (peak season in July).
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 18:30. Participate in a free camp-organized wildlife talk or documentary screening about the Maasai Mara ecosystem. Wind down with a hot cup of Kenyan tea.

meals.breakfast: Early camp breakfast — eggs, toast, and fruit — budget KES 300–400.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic box from camp eaten in the reserve — sandwiches, juice, and snacks — budget KES 300–450.
meals.dinner: Camp dinner: grilled tilapia or chicken with kachumbari salad and ugali — budget KES 700–1000.

day_by_day.notes: Full-day shared game drives cost approximately KES 3,500–5,500 per person including park fees. Always confirm what is included in the price. The Mara River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in until 07:30. After breakfast, explore the camp's surrounding area on a guided bird-watching walk. The Mara is home to over 450 bird species including lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and African fish eagles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget afternoon game drive (half-day shared drive, approximately KES 1,500–2,500 per person) focusing on the Talek River area. Look for hippo pods and crocodiles basking in the afternoon sun along the riverbanks.
day_by_day.evening: Camp social evening — connect with other budget travelers at the communal area. Share travel tips and experiences. Many camps organize informal cultural evenings with Maasai guides sharing stories around the fire.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely camp breakfast — pancakes, honey, and chai — budget KES 350–500.
meals.lunch: Camp lunch: tomato soup and bread rolls — budget KES 200–350.
meals.dinner: Self-cooked group meal if camp facilities allow, or budget camp set menu — budget KES 500–800.

day_by_day.notes: A rest day mid-trip helps you recharge. Use this time to charge camera batteries, back up photos, and review your budget spending. Check in with your accommodation about any free or low-cost activities available.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive at 06:00 with a focus on the open Mara plains for lion pride activity. July is excellent for spotting large predator groups. Ask your guide to take you to lesser-visited areas of the reserve for a more exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning to camp, spend the early afternoon visiting a local Maasai market near Talek town (if market day aligns). Browse handmade beaded jewelry, woven baskets, and traditional crafts. Practice bargaining respectfully for budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost conservation talk organized by camp — many Mara camps partner with wildlife conservancies and offer guest lectures on anti-poaching efforts and wildlife conservation.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: boiled eggs, bread, and fresh mango — budget KES 300–400.
meals.lunch: Try local Talek town eatery for a budget plate of mukimo (mashed potatoes with greens) and stew — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Camp dinner: slow-cooked beef stew with rice and steamed vegetables — budget KES 700–900.

day_by_day.notes: Talek town is a short drive from most Mara camps. Always go with a camp guide or trusted driver. The local market is a great place to buy authentic, fairly priced crafts directly from Maasai artisans.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive at 05:45 targeting cheetah activity on the open plains. The Mara is one of the best places in Africa to see cheetahs hunting. Spend time observing elephant family groups at close range with your experienced guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp by 10:30. Afternoon visit to the Mara Conservancy information center (if accessible from your camp) to learn about wildlife management and the ecosystem. Many conservancies offer free or low-cost educational visits.
day_by_day.evening: Outdoor camp dinner under the stars — many budget camps offer this experience periodically. Enjoy traditional Kenyan cuisine while listening to the sounds of the African night — distant lion roars and hyena calls.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: uji (porridge) with milk and sugar, fresh fruit — budget KES 250–350.
meals.lunch: Light camp lunch: avocado and tomato sandwiches — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Special outdoor bush dinner at camp — budget set menu KES 800–1200.

day_by_day.notes: Keep all food and drinks inside tents at night as wildlife including hyenas and baboons can be attracted to food smells. Always follow camp safety guidelines when outside after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Final early game drive in the Maasai Mara at 06:00. Focus on capturing final wildlife photographs and soaking in the last moments of the savanna. Look for the wildebeest migration herds and any remaining Big Five species you may have missed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of your boutique stay. Begin the journey toward Naivasha or Nakuru (approximately 3–4 hours by shared transport). Enjoy the scenic drive past the Rift Valley lakes. Arrive and check into a budget guesthouse in Naivasha (KES 1,500–2,500 per night).
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening walk along the shores of Lake Naivasha. The lake is famous for its hippo population and over 350 bird species. Watch the sunset over the water from a budget lakeside spot.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before checkout — eggs, toast, and tea — budget KES 300–400.
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a local town restaurant en route — githeri (corn and beans) or pilau rice — budget KES 150–250.
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local Naivasha restaurant: grilled tilapia from the lake with ugali and vegetables — budget KES 400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared matatu or shuttle from Narok to Naivasha in advance. The journey passes through beautiful Rift Valley scenery. Naivasha is significantly cheaper than the Mara for accommodation and food.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat ride on Lake Naivasha (budget shared boat approximately KES 800–1,200 per person). Spot hippos, African fish eagles, pelicans, and cormorants up close. Visit Crescent Island Game Sanctuary for a walking safari among zebras and giraffes — no predators, making it safe on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hell's Gate National Park — one of Kenya's most budget-friendly parks (entry KES 1,500 for non-residents or check current rates). Rent a bicycle (KES 500–800) and cycle through the dramatic gorge surrounded by towering cliffs, hot springs, and abundant wildlife including zebra and buffalo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Naivasha town. Explore the local evening market for fresh produce and street food. Relax at your guesthouse and prepare for the final day of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast: mandazi, chai, and boiled eggs — budget KES 200–300.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside snacks near Hell's Gate — roasted maize, samosas, and juice — budget KES 150–250.
meals.dinner: Local Naivasha restaurant dinner: nyama choma platter with kachumbari and chips — budget KES 500–700.

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate National Park is one of the few Kenyan parks where you can walk and cycle freely without a guide, making it extremely budget-friendly. The geothermal gorge walk is a must-do — wear sturdy shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk along Lake Naivasha shores for last-minute wildlife and bird spotting. Visit the local Elsamere Conservation Centre (former home of Joy Adamson of Born Free fame) — budget entry fee approximately KES 500. Learn about Kenya's conservation history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin journey back to Nairobi (approximately 1.5–2 hours by shared matatu, KES 200–300). Arrive in Nairobi with time to explore the budget-friendly Nairobi National Museum or browse the Maasai Market at Village Market for final souvenir shopping. Head to the airport for departure preparations.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Nairobi before heading to the airport. Enjoy a classic Kenyan farewell meal. Depart with incredible wildlife memories and a deep appreciation for Kenya's natural wonders.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse final breakfast: fresh fruit, bread, and Kenyan coffee — budget KES 200–300.
meals.lunch: Quick Nairobi lunch at a local café: samosa platter and fresh juice — budget KES 250–400.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Nairobi restaurant: Kenyan mixed grill or coastal biryani — budget KES 800–1200.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at JKIA. Keep some KES for airport taxes or last-minute purchases. Consider buying a bag of Kenyan coffee or tea as an affordable and authentic souvenir.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Nairobi/JKIA to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by charter flight). Settle into your boutique stay upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique lodge in Maasai Mara. Freshen up, enjoy a welcome drink, and receive a full orientation briefing from your guide about the reserve, safety protocols, and the week's game drive schedule. Take a short, relaxed walk around the lodge grounds to acclimatize.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the lodge terrace or a designated viewpoint near the camp. Watch the golden savannah light fade over the Mara plains. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the lodge with fellow guests and staff.

meals.breakfast: Snack or meal on the flight/during transfer
meals.lunch: Light packed lunch or roadside stop during transfer (budget KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique lodge — expect traditional Kenyan dishes such as nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, and sukuma wiki. Mid-range lodge dinner included or ~KES 2,500–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Arrive well-rested if possible. Carry a light jacket as Mara evenings can drop to 12–15°C. Confirm your game drive schedule with the lodge. Currency: have Kenyan Shillings (KES) handy for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day game drive in Maasai Mara National Reserve departing at 06:00. Focus on the northern Mara Triangle and Mara River crossings — prime territory for the Great Migration. Spot wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles gathering near the river. Look for lion prides and cheetahs on the open plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the Mara ecosystem. Visit the Mara River crossing points where dramatic wildebeest crossings often occur between July and October. Enjoy a bush picnic lunch prepared by the lodge served on the savannah — a quintessential Kenyan safari experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by 18:30 before darkness. Sundowner drinks on the terrace with views of the plains. Debrief with your guide about the day's wildlife sightings. Dinner at the lodge restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full safari breakfast at the lodge before departure — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, tea/coffee (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch provided by the lodge on the savannah (~KES 1,800–2,200 or included in safari package)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique lodge — grilled tilapia or chicken stew with local vegetables (~KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-coloured clothing (khaki, olive, beige) — avoid bright colours and white. Bring binoculars, sunscreen SPF 50+, a hat, and a camera with a zoom lens. The Great Migration peak is July–August — excellent timing for river crossings.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Great Migration Safari — focused morning game drive (06:00–10:00) targeting the wildebeest herds. Your guide will use radio contact with other drivers to locate active river crossings. This is one of the most dramatic wildlife spectacles on Earth — millions of animals moving in a continuous cycle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Cultural Village and Bush Walk experience. After lunch, visit a traditional Maasai manyatta village near the reserve boundary. Participate in a guided cultural tour — learn about Maasai warrior traditions, jumping dances, beadwork, and cattle herding practices. Enjoy a guided bush walk with a Maasai warrior guide who explains medicinal plants and tracking techniques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge. Optional campfire gathering with storytelling by Maasai guides. Purchase authentic handmade Maasai beadwork and crafts directly from the village artisans (budget KES 500–3,000 depending on items).

meals.breakfast: Full safari breakfast at the lodge (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge restaurant — try the Kenyan beef stew or vegetable curry with chapati (~KES 1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — barbecue night with nyama choma, roasted vegetables, and fresh salads (~KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Ask permission before photographing Maasai community members — a small tip or craft purchase is appreciated. The bush walk is approximately 2–3 km on flat terrain. Wear closed-toe shoes and long trousers for the walk.

day_by_day.morning: Optional hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at dawn (pre-book in advance — approximately USD 450–500 per person, a splurge worth considering for the experience). Float over the golden plains watching wildlife from above at sunrise. Alternatively, early morning game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, leopards, and hyenas are most active at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon at the lodge. Enjoy the pool or lounge area. Optional guided nature walk around the lodge perimeter with a naturalist guide to spot birds, insects, and smaller wildlife. The Mara is home to over 450 bird species — bring a bird checklist.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner game drive (16:00–18:30) — the golden hour light is perfect for photography. Focus on elephant herds, hippos at the river, and big cat activity as dusk approaches. Return for dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field after the balloon safari, or full lodge breakfast (~KES 1,500 or included)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge — fresh salads, sandwiches, and fruit (~KES 1,200–1,800)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at the lodge — three-course meal with Kenyan-inspired cuisine including avocado salad, grilled chicken, and passion fruit dessert (~KES 3,000–4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be booked at least 2–3 days in advance through the lodge. Weather in July is warm (25°C) with minimal rain (30mm monthly) — ideal conditions for ballooning. Carry a fleece for the cold morning balloon ride.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara early (07:00) for Lake Nakuru National Park — approximately 3.5–4 hours drive north via Narok town. En route, enjoy scenic views of the Great Rift Valley escarpment. Arrive at Lake Nakuru by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Five Safari. Afternoon game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage site. The alkaline lake is famous for its spectacular flocks of lesser and greater flamingos turning the shoreline pink. Look for white rhinos, lions, leopards, buffaloes, and giraffes in the acacia and euphorbia forests surrounding the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge or tented camp near Lake Nakuru (pre-booked). Freshen up and enjoy dinner at the lodge. Watch the sunset over the Rift Valley from an elevated viewpoint near the park.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Mara lodge before departure (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during the drive or stop at a roadside restaurant in Narok town — try pilau rice and grilled chicken (~KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lake Nakuru lodge — fresh tilapia from Lake Victoria or beef stew with ugali (~KES 2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: The drive passes through Narok town — a good place for a fuel stop and to buy fresh fruit from roadside vendors. Lake Nakuru park fees: approximately USD 60–80 per person per day. Keep windows up near baboon-populated areas.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park (06:30–10:30). Focus on the lake shore for flamingo photography and the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for panoramic views of the entire lake. Look for the endangered Rothschild's giraffe — Lake Nakuru is a key sanctuary for this subspecies. Rhino tracking with park rangers is a highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 2.5–3 hours north towards Laikipia Plateau). Check in to a mid-range camp at Ol Pejeta. Afternoon guided game drive in the conservancy — home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth (Najin and Fatu), the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa, and a thriving population of lions, elephants, and chimpanzees.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the northern white rhino enclosure before closing time (17:00) — a profoundly moving conservation experience. Attend an evening conservation talk at the Ol Pejeta visitor centre about rhino protection efforts. Dinner at the camp.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light meal at a roadside stop en route to Ol Pejeta (~KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp — hearty safari meal with soup, main course, and dessert (~KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy entry: approximately USD 90–110 per person per day (includes rhino tracking). The northern white rhino visit is emotionally significant — there are only 2 left in the world. Photography is encouraged to raise awareness.

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — early morning guided rhino tracking experience (06:00–09:00) with expert trackers on foot or in a vehicle. Learn about the intensive 24-hour security operations protecting the rhinos. Track black rhinos through the bush — a rare and thrilling wildlife encounter. Also look for lions, leopards, and the conservancy's chimpanzee sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon game drive in Ol Pejeta. The conservancy borders Mount Kenya and offers stunning mountain backdrop scenery. Look for large elephant herds, Cape buffaloes, Grevy's zebras, and reticulated giraffes — species not seen in the Mara. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary for a guided chimp viewing session (unique in Kenya).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the plains. Return to camp for dinner and a night game drive (optional, approximately USD 30–40 extra) — spot nocturnal species including aardvarks, genets, and bush babies.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before rhino tracking — coffee, toast, and fruit (included or ~KES 1,000)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Ol Pejeta picnic site or camp restaurant — grilled meats and salads (~KES 1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at camp — wood-fired pizza night or traditional Kenyan buffet (~KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Rhino tracking requires a minimum fitness level for the walking component. Wear subdued colours and follow tracker instructions carefully. The chimpanzee sanctuary visit requires advance booking — confirm with the conservancy.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta early (07:00) and drive south to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours via Nairobi bypass). En route, enjoy the scenic transition from the Laikipia highlands down through the Rift Valley. Arrive at Amboseli by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop. Afternoon game drive in Amboseli National Park — one of Africa's most iconic wildlife destinations. Amboseli is famous for its large elephant herds roaming against the backdrop of snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895m). The afternoon light is ideal for photography with the mountain visible in clear weather.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge or eco-camp near Amboseli. Sundowner from Observation Hill — a volcanic outcrop with 360° views of the park, Kilimanjaro, and the vast swamps where elephants gather at dusk. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp before departure (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Stop in Nairobi for lunch at a mid-range restaurant — try Carnivore Restaurant for grilled game meats or a local nyama choma spot (~KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge — enjoy fresh Kenyan cuisine with Kilimanjaro views (~KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli park fees: approximately USD 60–80 per person per day. July mornings offer the clearest views of Kilimanjaro before clouds build. Amboseli's swamps attract enormous elephant herds — the park hosts some of Africa's most studied elephant families.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in Amboseli National Park (06:00–10:30). Focus on the Enkongo Narok and Longinye swamps where elephant herds numbering 50–100+ animals gather to feed and bathe. Amboseli's elephants are habituated to vehicles and allow very close approaches — extraordinary for photography. Also look for lions, cheetahs, and large herds of wildebeest and zebras.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk with a Maasai guide around the lodge perimeter and into the park buffer zone. Learn about Amboseli's unique ecosystem — a mosaic of swamps, woodlands, and open plains fed by underground streams from Kilimanjaro's glaciers. Visit a nearby Maasai community project that benefits from conservation tourism.
day_by_day.evening: Final Amboseli sundowner game drive (16:00–18:30). Capture the iconic image of elephant silhouettes against the golden glow of Kilimanjaro at sunset. Return for a celebratory farewell dinner at the lodge with your guide.

meals.breakfast: Full safari breakfast at the lodge (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the park near the swamps — watching elephants while eating is an unforgettable experience (lodge-prepared, ~KES 1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the lodge — three-course meal celebrating the end of the safari. Try Kenyan lamb chops with roasted sweet potatoes (~KES 3,000–4,500)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's elephant population includes some of the oldest matriarchs in Africa — ask your guide about the famous Echo family documented by Cynthia Moss. Carry dust protection for cameras as Amboseli is drier and dustier than the Mara.

day_by_day.morning: Early final game drive in Amboseli (05:30–08:00) for last wildlife sightings and sunrise photography with Kilimanjaro. Return to the lodge for a full breakfast. Pack up and check out. Depart Amboseli for Nairobi (approximately 4 hours drive) or transfer to Amboseli airstrip for a charter flight to Nairobi Wilson Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi by midday. Depending on your departure flight timing, visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre (Rothschild's giraffe conservation — USD 15 entry) or the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (free, donations welcome). Both are located near Wilson Airport and make excellent final wildlife experiences. Transfer to JKIA for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi JKIA. If your flight departs late evening, enjoy a final dinner at a Nairobi restaurant — try Talisman Restaurant in Karen (mid-range, ~KES 3,000–4,500) or Brew Bistro in Westlands for a relaxed farewell meal.

meals.breakfast: Full farewell breakfast at Amboseli lodge (included or ~KES 1,500)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi — Karen Blixen Coffee Garden near the museum offers a lovely mid-range option (~KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or final Nairobi restaurant meal before departure (~KES 2,000–4,500 depending on choice)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for JKIA check-in and security. Purchase any remaining Kenyan souvenirs at Nairobi's Maasai Market (open daily) or the airport duty-free. Keep USD 50 in cash for airport tips and incidentals. Confirm return transfer bookings the day before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive in open 4x4 vehicles to observe predator-prey interactions, lion prides, cheetahs, and elephants in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds, with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop. Spot hippos at Observation Hill, flamingos at Lake Amboseli, and diverse birdlife while experienced guides share deep knowledge of elephant family dynamics and ecosystems.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Participate in a guided rhino tracking experience on foot or by vehicle, meet rescued chimpanzees at the Jane Goodall sanctuary, and learn about critical conservation efforts protecting endangered species.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Five Safari
experiences.description: Discover Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its stunning flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park also offers excellent Big Five sightings including white and black rhinos, lions, leopards, and buffalos. Enjoy scenic viewpoints over the lake from Baboon Cliff for breathtaking panoramic photography.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village and Bush Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided visit to a traditional manyatta village near the Mara. Participate in traditional jumping dances, learn about ancient herding customs, medicinal plant knowledge, and beadwork craftsmanship. Follow a Maasai warrior guide on a bush walk to learn how indigenous communities have coexisted with wildlife for centuries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, you will be welcomed by a private luxury transfer service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury vehicle transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours via the scenic Narok road). En route, enjoy curated snack boxes and chilled beverages prepared by your lodge. Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara as the golden hour sets in. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the lodge grounds with a resident naturalist.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome sundowner cocktails on the lodge's viewing deck overlooking the savannah, followed by a private welcome dinner under the stars with your personal butler. The chef presents a curated Kenyan-fusion tasting menu featuring local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.lunch: Gourmet snack hamper and beverages provided in the private transfer vehicle
meals.dinner: Private open-air welcome dinner at the boutique lodge — Kenyan-fusion tasting menu with locally sourced meats, seasonal vegetables, and artisan desserts, paired with South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your passport and visa documents are ready for immigration. The lodge team will coordinate all luggage handling. Lightweight layers are recommended for the evening as temperatures can drop to around 15°C on the Mara.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 05:30 for the signature Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari. Board a custom open-sided 4x4 Land Cruiser with your private guide and tracker. Witness the extraordinary spectacle of millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles moving across the Mara plains. Prime viewing of river crossings at the Mara River, where crocodiles and hippos await — one of nature's most dramatic events.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a lavish bush brunch. After a brief rest, embark on an afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are highly active in the Mara during July. Visit the Mara Triangle for exceptional big cat sightings and expansive views of the migration herds.
day_by_day.evening: Guided bush walk at dusk with a Maasai warrior escort to learn about nocturnal wildlife and star navigation. Return for a candlelit dinner at the lodge's private boma (traditional enclosure) with a live Maasai cultural performance.

meals.breakfast: Early-morning packed gourmet breakfast box in the vehicle — freshly brewed coffee, pastries, seasonal fruit, and boiled eggs
meals.lunch: Lavish bush brunch at the lodge — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, tropical fruits, artisan cheeses, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Private boma dinner — slow-roasted game meats, grilled vegetables, ugali (Kenyan polenta), and traditional Kenyan stews, with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Bring binoculars, a high-quality camera with a telephoto lens, and insect repellent. The Great Migration river crossings are unpredictable — your guide will use real-time radio networks to position you at the best vantage points.

day_by_day.morning: Hot air balloon safari at sunrise over the Maasai Mara — a breathtaking perspective of the migration herds, predators, and the vast savannah from above. Float silently for approximately one hour as the sun rises over the Mara ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional champagne bush breakfast after landing, a classic Kenyan safari tradition. Return to the lodge for a midday wellness session — choose from a bush massage, yoga on the deck, or a guided meditation session overlooking the plains. Optional afternoon game drive targeting the elusive leopard and the resident cheetah coalitions.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private sundowner at a scenic Mara hilltop with your guide and butler — enjoy artisan canapés, chilled champagne, and a curated charcuterie board as the sun dips below the horizon. Return for a relaxed à la carte dinner at the lodge's main dining pavilion.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the field after the balloon landing — full English spread with smoked meats, eggs, fruits, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light à la carte lunch at the lodge — avocado salad, grilled tilapia, and tropical sorbet
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the lodge dining pavilion — pan-seared Mara lamb, roasted root vegetables, and dark chocolate fondant with Kenyan coffee

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon experience must be booked in advance and is weather-dependent. Flights typically launch at 06:00. Wear warm layers for the balloon ride as temperatures at altitude can be cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Cultural Village and Bush Walk experience. Depart after a leisurely breakfast for an immersive visit to an authentic Maasai manyatta (village). Meet the community elders, learn about traditional customs, beadwork, and the warrior lifestyle. Participate in a traditional jumping ceremony and browse handcrafted Maasai jewellery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided bush walk led by an expert Maasai tracker and a professional naturalist. Learn to identify animal tracks, medicinal plants, and the intricate ecosystem of the Mara on foot — an intimate and exhilarating way to experience the wilderness. Return to the lodge for a refreshing dip in the pool and afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-room dining experience — your butler sets up an elegant table on your private suite terrace. The chef delivers a personalised five-course menu tailored to your preferences, served under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — freshly baked breads, tropical fruit platters, eggs cooked to order, Kenyan chai, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch during the walking safari — gourmet sandwiches, wraps, fresh fruit, and chilled lemonade served in a shaded acacia grove
meals.dinner: Private terrace five-course dinner — amuse-bouche, roasted butternut soup, pan-seared Nile perch, Kenyan-spiced tenderloin, and a mango panna cotta dessert, with sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-coloured, closed-toe shoes for the bush walk. The Maasai village visit includes a small community contribution fee that supports local education and conservation projects.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Lake Nakuru National Park — depart early by private charter flight or luxury 4x4 (approximately 3 hours by road). Upon arrival, begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Five Safari. Witness thousands of lesser and greater flamingos painting the lake pink, alongside white rhinos, lions, leopards, and large herds of buffalo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Lake Nakuru game drive, focusing on the park's resident Rothschild's giraffes — one of the world's most endangered giraffe subspecies. Visit the lake's southern shore for the best flamingo density and birdwatching. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your lodge team at a scenic lakeside viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Maasai Mara. Arrive at the lodge in time for a relaxing evening. Unwind with a therapeutic bush spa treatment — a signature Mara mineral body scrub or hot stone massage using locally sourced botanicals.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the lodge before departure — pastries, fruit, yoghurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lakeside picnic at Lake Nakuru — smoked salmon blinis, artisan cheese boards, cold cuts, and sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Casual lodge dinner — wood-fired pizza with Kenyan toppings, garden salad, and a selection of East African craft beers and wines

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Flamingo numbers vary seasonally — July typically offers excellent sightings. Bring a wide-angle lens for landscape and bird photography. The park also has excellent rhino viewing opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Maasai Mara to Amboseli National Park (approximately 45 minutes by air). Check in to a luxury tented camp with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop experience — observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming the open plains with the snow-capped peak as a dramatic backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in Amboseli focusing on the park's diverse birdlife and predator activity. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic 360-degree view of the park, the swamps, and Kilimanjaro. Spot large elephant bulls, hippos in the Amboseli swamps, and large flocks of pelicans and herons.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at Observation Hill with your private guide. Return to the tented camp for a welcome dinner featuring Kenyan coastal cuisine — a nod to the Swahili culinary traditions of East Africa.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Mara lodge before the flight — eggs, fresh fruit, and Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Amboseli tented camp — grilled chicken, roasted vegetables, and a fresh garden salad
meals.dinner: Kenyan coastal dinner at the camp — Swahili-spiced grilled prawns, coconut fish curry, pilau rice, and kachumbari (fresh tomato salsa), with East African wines

day_by_day.notes: Kilimanjaro views are best in the early morning before clouds build — plan your first game drive accordingly. Amboseli is renowned for the best elephant photography in Africa due to the open terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive in Amboseli — the golden morning light against Kilimanjaro creates extraordinary photographic opportunities. A private professional wildlife photographer guide accompanies you to capture the perfect elephant silhouettes. Visit the famous Amboseli elephant families studied by the Amboseli Elephant Research Project — one of the longest-running wildlife studies in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit to a local Maasai community near Amboseli for a cultural exchange — learn about their coexistence with wildlife and conservation efforts. Return to camp for a leisurely afternoon with access to the swimming pool, spa, and library. Optional guided nature walk around the camp's buffer zone.
day_by_day.evening: Private candlelit dinner in the bush — your camp team sets up an exclusive table in the wilderness with lanterns, fine linens, and a personalised menu. A violinist or local musician provides ambient entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast during the morning game drive — thermos coffee, freshly baked scones, and fruit
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the camp — Caesar salad, grilled fish tacos, and freshly pressed juices
meals.dinner: Exclusive bush dinner — five-course menu featuring wild mushroom velouté, Amboseli-inspired game terrine, grilled beef tenderloin, and a passion fruit tart, with Kenyan sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: The Amboseli elephant families are individually named and studied — your guide can introduce you to specific family groups. Early morning light (06:00–08:00) offers the best Kilimanjaro visibility before cloud cover develops.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia (approximately 1 hour by air). Check in to the luxury conservancy lodge. Begin the Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience — a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with Sudan's legacy: the last two northern white rhinos on Earth (Najin and Fatu), under 24-hour armed guard protection. Meet the dedicated rangers who protect them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extensive game drive across Ol Pejeta — home to the largest black rhino population in East Africa, as well as lions, leopards, elephants, and chimpanzees at the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary. Visit the sanctuary for a guided tour and learn about the rehabilitation of rescued chimpanzees.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the conservancy's signature restaurant with views over the floodlit waterhole — watch wildlife come to drink as you dine. A conservation expert joins your table for an exclusive talk on Ol Pejeta's pioneering rhino protection and IVF research programmes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli camp before the flight — full cooked breakfast with fresh fruits and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Ol Pejeta lodge — light sandwiches, soups, and a cheese board
meals.dinner: Waterhole-view dinner at the lodge restaurant — slow-cooked Laikipia lamb shank, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a dark chocolate and Amarula mousse, paired with premium Kenyan and South African wines

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino encounter requires advance booking through Ol Pejeta Conservancy and includes a conservation contribution fee. Photography is permitted but flash is strictly prohibited near the rhinos. Bring a warm jacket — Laikipia is at higher altitude and evenings can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning horseback safari across the Ol Pejeta plains — an extraordinary way to move silently through wildlife with zebras, giraffes, and antelopes. Suitable for all riding abilities with professional guides. Experience the African bush from a completely different perspective as animals remain calm around horses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a farewell brunch. Private charter flight back to Nairobi (approximately 45 minutes). Check in to a luxury Nairobi hotel (Hemingways Nairobi or The Emakoko recommended) for the final night. Afternoon at leisure — optional visit to the Giraffe Centre or David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant nursery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants — Talisman Restaurant or Carnivore (game meat specialist) — celebrating an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan journey. Enjoy premium cocktails, live jazz, and a curated farewell menu.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast before the horseback safari
meals.lunch: Farewell brunch at Ol Pejeta lodge — smoked salmon, eggs royale, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner in Nairobi — premium game meat platter or à la carte fine dining, with a sommelier-curated wine flight and artisan dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: The David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant nursery visiting hours are 11:00–12:00 only — plan accordingly if you wish to visit. The Giraffe Centre allows you to hand-feed Rothschild's giraffes. Both are excellent final Nairobi experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Nairobi. Enjoy a luxurious hotel breakfast at your own pace. Last-minute curated shopping for premium Kenyan souvenirs — visit Kazuri Beads (fair-trade ceramic jewellery), Utamaduni Crafts Centre, or the Karen Blixen Museum gift shop for artisan keepsakes and locally produced coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure. Your concierge arranges fast-track check-in, luggage handling, and access to the VIP departure lounge with premium refreshments and Wi-Fi.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Kenya's most iconic wildlife destinations — the Maasai Mara, Amboseli, Lake Nakuru, and Ol Pejeta — with memories of the Great Migration, elephant herds beneath Kilimanjaro, and the world's last northern white rhinos.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit, eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, and specialty Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or airport VIP lounge — club sandwiches, fresh salads, and premium beverages
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for check-in and security at JKIA. Your concierge can arrange duty-free Kenyan coffee, tea, and wine purchases. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no ivory, rhino horn, or protected species products.
